Message to U.S. Citizens: Small-Scale Anti-U.S. Protests Expected near the U.S. Embassy on Friday, February 6, 2026
https://t.co/PuT73N7sc0

Location: Near U.S. Embassy along Kalaw Avenue in Manila
Event: Small-Scale Anti-U.S. Protests Expected near the U.S. Embassy on Friday, February 6, 2026

The protest is scheduled for Friday, February 6, 2026.  The group will assemble along Kalaw Avenue at 9:30 a.m. and begin marching toward the Embassy at approximately 9:45 a.m. with approximately 50-100 expected attendees.  The protest will include a range of organizations and associations, from the Philippines-Palestine Friendship Association to the Philippines-Bolivarian Venezuela Friendship Association, calling for action against “U.S. Imperialist Wars and Fascism.”

Actions to Take:
· U.S. citizens should avoid the rallies, as even peaceful rallies/demonstrations have the potential to turn violent without warning. Foreign nationals found engaging in a protest or mass demonstration could be considered in violation of their immigration status.
· Monitor local media and government sources for updates on possible disruptions and re-routing schemes as heavy traffic congestion and road closures are expected near protest venues.
· Follow instructions from local authorities.
· Exercise caution when in the vicinity of any large gatherings.
----------------------------------------------------------

For further information and assistance:
· Enroll in the Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (STEP) (https://t.co/q8w0nZfWZo) to receive Alerts and make it easier to locate you in an emergency.
· Contact the U.S. Embassy in Manila, Philippines, located at 1201 Roxas Boulevard, at +(63) (2) 5301-2000, from 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday through Friday. After-hours emergency number for U.S. citizens is +(63) (2) 5301-2000.
· Call 1-888-407-4747 toll-free in the United States and Canada or 1-202-501-4444 from other countries from 8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. Eastern Standard Time, Monday through Friday (except U.S. federal holidays).
· See the State Department’s travel website (https://t.co/Tiyt8sq7F9) for the Worldwide Caution, Travel Advisories, Alerts, and the Philippines Country Specific Information (https://t.co/ApMa3LxNZy).
